theFix.chosen: size the service container's lock table; the harness is NOT changed and --shm-size is NOT set
theFix.theOneStep: A new step in the `test` job named `Size the postgres lock table for the test suite`, at index 8 of 16 steps, before all five database-touching steps (Enable pgvector, Install postgis, Enable postgis, Push database schema, Run tests -- asserted by parsing, see workflowStructure). It runs `docker ps --filter ancestor=pgvector/pgvector:pg14`, FAILS CLOSED unless exactly one container matches, runs `ALTER SYSTEM SET max_locks_per_transaction = 1024`, restarts the container with `docker restart --time 60`, waits for a real `SELECT 1` (up to 120s), READS THE EFFECTIVE VALUE BACK, PRINTS IT ON EVERY RUN, and exits 1 if it is not 1024.
theFix.whyOneStepIsTheWholeFix: The lock table is a shared cluster-wide resource and the operations that overrun it (one `DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE`, and one 616-statement CREATE in a single implicit transaction) are legitimate and stay as they are. Sizing the resource fixes every concurrent DB suite at once -- including local runs against any container started the same way -- and imposes no cap on test parallelism, which batching the drops would have.
theFix.nothingElseChanged: No test, no harness function, no other workflow, and no `services.options`. In particular --shm-size is untouched because it was MEASURED not to move the ceiling: lock capacity is identical (12,800) at 64 MB and at 2 GB of /dev/shm, an equal 12-way load fails on both, and 1024 starts and passes on the stock 64 MB /dev/shm. The lock table is anonymous shared memory, not /dev/shm, so a larger --shm-size can never clear this error; only the GUC sizes it, and the GUC is PGC_POSTMASTER, hence the restart.
theFix.whyNotDeclarative: A job in a service container cannot be given the GUC declaratively: `services.options` is passed to `docker create` and there is no command override, so the step must ALTER SYSTEM + restart. Named in leave_behind as the thing that would make this declarative if the platform ever gains one.

leave_behind: If the platform ever lets a service container take a command or an env override, this step becomes declarative (`services.postgres.command: postgres -c max_locks_per_transaction=1024`) and the ALTER SYSTEM + restart + read-back can be deleted. Worth taking the day it exists; the restart is the only expensive part of the step (~3s, plus a window in which postgres is briefly unreachable).

max_locks_per_transaction is PGC_POSTMASTER, so any future size change requires that restart dance. If a suite ever legitimately needs more than ~190,000 locks, raise TARGET; the step prints the effective value so the need will be visible before it becomes a red.

`artifacts/smartsite-mcp` cannot run against a freshly pushed database in a local full-workspace run: its tests delete from `engagements`, which does not exist, so `pnpm test` aborts there (42P01). CI passes because it gets there through a different path. A local seat trying to reproduce a whole-workspace failure will hit this first and could mistake it for the thing they were chasing -- it is a local precondition gap and it wants fixing or documenting.

On Windows, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` at this repo fails at the root `preinstall` (`sh -c ...`) because pnpm runs scripts through cmd.exe; setting `npm_config_script_shell` to Git Bash fixes it and the install then completes from the store in seconds. It looks like a repo defect and is not.

scratch.LESSON: `set -e` + `set -o pipefail` + `VAR=$(cmd | filter)` means a failing `cmd` aborts the whole script, because an assignment whose command substitution fails is itself a failed command. A polling loop written that way only works when it is not needed -- every retry after the first is unreachable. Write `VAR=$(cmd | filter || true)` inside a poll loop, and test the loop by making its FIRST attempt fail.

`pg_isready` is not readiness. A server in crash recovery answers the socket with 'rejecting connections' long before it can execute anything, so a `pg_isready` gate passes/fails at the wrong moment. Poll a real query.

`docker restart` defaults to a 10s SIGTERM budget; a busy postgres that has not finished its fast shutdown in 10s gets SIGKILLed, and an unclean stop forces WAL replay on the NEXT start (measured here: 20.5s of redo plus a stall, every connection refused as 'the database system is starting up'). Use `--time 60` where a clean stop matters.
